newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ sees China cutting wool tariff after Zhu visit.
newsitem.headline: NZ sees China cutting wool tariff after Zhu visit.

text.p: China's tariffs on New Zealand wool should fall soon, Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Tuesday after talks with China's visiting Vice Premier Zhu Rongji.
"The vice premier talked about the level of the tariff (on wool)," Bolger told reporters.
"The ambition on the part of China...is to lower the tariffs for wool along with other commodities and to do that reasonably soon so (New Zealand exports) will be going in over a lower tariff."
New Zealand faces formal tariffs into China of 20 percent on tops (processed wool for yarns) and 15 percent on raw wool.
But for imports within a quota the rate falls to around five percent on tops and three percent on wool.
After the talks New Zealand officials said they expected the broader tariff rates to fall to the quota tariff level in time.
Zhu, who is on a five-day visit to New Zealand, told journalists he agreed with Bolger's assessment of the issue.
"I fully agree with the prime minister's opinions. We have had very good talks with the prime minister and ministers and I think we have no debate (disagreement)," Zhu said.

Bolger said the talks had covered specific trade issues including New Zealand's desire to re-establish its kiwifruit trade back into China after a fruitfly scare and its hopes for improved access for wool, where China is its biggest customer.
The countries' two-way direct trade is worth over NZ$1.30 billion ($900 million) a year, though Bolger noted the balance was in China's favour.
"We would like to change that, of course, and they would like to keep it," he added.
New Zealand has said it is keen to encourage more processed exports into the Chinese market and also wants to see growth in trade in services.
